records.name: Energy Justice Network
records.summary: An advocacy group that opposes polluting energy and waste facilities and promotes zero waste, wind, solar, and energy storage. It maps facilities nationwide and helps local residents organize against threats in their own communities.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for news and activism invitations, join an issue email list, help research or write fact sheets, or help map polluting facilities. The group also takes applications for its board and asks people who want to be members to send a pledge form.

schedule.text: No meetings or regular gatherings are listed on the site. News posts and campaigns run through the year.

cost.text: The member services page says joining is free. Donations are invited.

first_step.how: Fill in the sign-up form on energyjustice.net with your name, contact details, ZIP, and the kinds of help you want, or email niaby@energyjustice.net to ask about joining a list or helping with research.
first_step.basis: The sign-up form and the Get Involved page are public and list several clear ways in, but the site lists no meetings and does not say what happens after you sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit, and it lists no meetings, events, or drop-in times. Signing up adds you to the group's news and invitations, and the form asks which kinds of help interest you. Phone and email are the other ways in that the site names.
first_visit_tips: Name the local threat you care about in the form's comment box, which takes up to 180 characters.
Ask by email or phone which meetings are open to new people before you plan a trip to 1434 Elbridge St, since the site does not say whether the office takes visitors.

records.notes: The member services page says joining is free, but it describes member groups (grassroots organizations), so an individual should confirm before assuming the same terms. The Get Involved page asks would-be members to complete a pledge form. Newest dated post is April 22, 2026. The Mapping Project and JusticeMap.org are tools the group runs, not separate groups, so they are not leads. The Center for Health, Environment and Justice is named as a resource, appears to be a national group, and was not listed.

records.name: Enon Tabernacle Baptist Church
records.summary: A Baptist church with two Philadelphia locations: Enon East on West Cheltenham Avenue and Enon West on West Coulter Street. Neighbors can join Sunday worship at either campus, a Thursday night young adult Bible study, or a young adult fellowship that meets the second weekend of each month.
records.what_you_do: Attend Sunday worship at either campus, join the Thursday young adult Bible study at Enon East, or take part in the young adult gatherings held on the second weekend of each month, where young adults also lead some worship services.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 6:45 am at Enon West and 9:45 am at Enon East. Thursday young adult Bible study at 7 pm at Enon East. Young adult gatherings are on the second weekend of each month, with no set dates shown.

cost.text: No fee is listed on the church's pages. Giving is available online.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at either campus. To join the Thursday young adult Bible study, register through the Online Registration link on enonbiblewalk.org or call (215) 276-7200.
first_step.basis: The About page says the doors are open to anyone seeking connection or spiritual growth, and the homepage gives a phone line and a registration link for the Bible study.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship happens at two campuses, at 6:45 am at Enon West and 9:45 am at Enon East. The site does not say how long a service runs or what it is like inside, so call the church office if you want those details first. Young adults lead some worship services, and a Thursday 7 pm Bible study meets at Enon East.
first_visit_tips: Check the Calendar page on the church website, which the church also keeps in its app.
Call (215) 276-7200 or email enon@enontab.org with questions before a first visit.
Pick the campus that fits your morning: 6:45 am at Enon West or 9:45 am at Enon East.

records.notes: The announcements page lists October items with registration links, including a New Member Intensive and a Pre-Baptism meeting, but the text gives no year, so no last_sign_of_life was set. Several image-only items show 2026 only in their file names, and those were not used. The Join Enon and Young Adults pages returned 404, so the membership route is only known through the registration link. The calendar page's event listing did not load in the fetch, so no dated events were recorded. The site gives no parking, access, or ASL details.

records.name: Entrepreneur Works
records.summary: A nonprofit lender and business coach for small businesses in Philadelphia and Chester. It runs workshops and business-start programs that the public can sign up for through its events calendar.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a workshop, join a business-start or pitch program, or ask the office about a small business loan or grant.

schedule.text: Workshops, short business events, and coaching sessions are listed on the events calendar. Coaching is by application, and availability changes through the year.

cost.text: Not stated on the site. Check each event page.

first_step.how: Pick a workshop on the upcoming events calendar and register on its page, or call the Philadelphia office at 215.545.3100 to ask about the Start It Grow It program.
first_step.basis: The site says it meets people where they are in experience, and its Start It Grow It program is aimed at people starting a business, with a clear way to register or call.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most sessions are short workshops on topics such as online marketing, managing money, and getting a loan, and you register on each event page. One-on-one coaching needs an application and depends on availability. The site does not give the length or cost of most sessions, so ask before you come.
first_visit_tips: Register on the event page before you go, since walk-ins are not described.
Call 215.545.3100 to ask the cost and the room for the session you want.
The contact page lists a second Philadelphia address, 400 Market Street, Suite 210, with no note on which is current, so confirm before you visit.

records.notes: The programs page describes Start It Grow It as a self-paced online course with enrollment open at any time, but the program's own page gives no format, length, or cost, so only what the programs page says is relied on. The only dated event on the calendar is a November 18, 2026 session, kept out of schedule text. The 2026-10 sign of life is the listing of that event on the upcoming events page. The evening time from tier 1 came from that one-time event and was removed. The Chester office phone is 267-792-3770. Loan and grant eligibility is not listed.

records.name: Epiphany of Our Lord Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 11th and Jackson Streets in South Philadelphia. It holds Sunday and weekday Masses, and some of its Masses have sign language interpreting, including a hearing-impaired Mass on the second and fourth Sundays.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, which is free and open to all. Sign language interpreting is used at some weekly or monthly liturgies, so ask the parish which Mass has it that week.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8:30 am in the Lower Church and 11 am in the Upper Church. Saturday Mass at 5 pm. Weekday Masses at 8 am or 8:30 am, depending on the day; the parish site and the archdiocese page list the weekday days differently, so call ahead. Confession Saturdays 4:15 to 4:45 pm.

access.notes: Sign language interpreting is provided at some weekly or monthly liturgies, per the archdiocese parish page. The parish site calls the 11 am Sunday Mass in the Upper Church on the second and fourth Sundays the hearing-impaired Mass.

first_step.how: Come to the 11 am Sunday Mass in the Upper Church on the second or fourth Sunday, the hearing-impaired Mass, or call 215-334-1035 to ask which Mass has interpreting that week.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and the parish phone line is listed, but the site has no page for newcomers or visitors.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and anyone can attend. The 11 am Sunday Mass in the Upper Church, on the second and fourth Sundays, is the one the parish calls its hearing-impaired Mass. Interpreting at other Masses varies by week, so call the parish before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-334-1035 to confirm which Mass has sign language interpreting that week.
Use the How to get here map on the parish website for directions.

records.notes: Weekday Mass days conflict between sources: the parish home page lists Tuesday to Saturday at 8:30 am, while the archdiocese parish page lists Monday to Saturday at 8 am with Tuesday at 8:30 am. Both are recorded as a range, and the record says to call ahead. The parish contact page returned 404. The archdiocese ASL page lists Epiphany but gives no days or times; the 11 am second and fourth Sunday detail comes from the parish's own site. The archdiocese deaf ministry page redirected to an unrelated domain and was not followed. The Knights of Columbus council is named on the parish events page as an external link; no council site was located, so it was not listed as a lead. The 2026 pasta dinner is a one-time event and was not recorded. Confession times are carried from tier 1 and were not re-read this pass.

records.name: Epiphany Singers
records.summary: A non-profit choir of young adults in Philadelphia that sings traditional and modern choral music. Singers join through an audition, and the choir holds Open Sing-Ins where people can sing with the group for a day.
records.what_you_do: Sing in the choir after an audition, or come to an Open Sing-In to try it for a day. Concerts are open to the public, and tickets are sold for some of them.

schedule.text: Rehearsals are on Saturdays from 1 to 3 pm at the Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul. Small ensembles may add extra rehearsals and performances.

locations.label: Rehearsals, concerts and Open Sing-Ins
locations.address: 1723 Race St (Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul)

cost.text: Concert tickets are sold for some concerts. Audition and Open Sing-In fees are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Complete the audition form on the audition page (name, age, voice part, email, and phone are required), or watch the events list for an Open Sing-In and sing with the choir for a day.
first_step.basis: The audition page says singers at any level are welcome and explains how to sign up. Membership is by audition, but Open Sing-Ins are a public one-day way to sing with the choir.
first_step.what_to_expect: The audition has five parts: a warm-up, a piece you choose, sight reading, pitch memory, and quartet singing, with the quartet scores and tracks provided before the audition. Members rehearse on Saturdays from 1 to 3 pm at the Cathedral Basilica. The site lists past audition dates but not the next one, and it gives no fee for auditions or Open Sing-Ins.
first_visit_tips: Prepare a piece that shows your best choral singing, since you choose it for the audition.
Watch the events list for the next Open Sing-In, since the site does not say what to bring.
Email epiphanysingersphila@gmail.com with questions about Open Sing-Ins or auditions.

records.notes: The homepage shows a contact address (info@wimpoletherapeautics.com) that does not appear to belong to the choir, so it was not used. Years on dated events come from the homepage, since the event list shows month and day only. The December 4, 2026 concert is kept out of schedule text. The Open Sing-In fee, what to bring, and whether first-time singers can attend without auditioning are not stated on any page read, so the record does not say they can. The audition page's 'any level' wording is what supports newcomer rating 4.

records.name: Esteem Girls
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs hands-on STEM activities for girls in grades 3 to 8, both after school and on Saturdays.
records.what_you_do: Girls do hands-on science, technology, engineering and math work with program staff. STEM Afterschool runs on weekdays from school dismissal to 6 pm, and STEM Saturday meets on second Saturdays. Afterschool pickup is offered from select schools. Adults can also volunteer as ambassadors, event helpers, guest speakers, or behind-the-scenes helpers.

schedule.text: STEM Afterschool runs Monday to Friday from school dismissal until 6 pm during the 2026 to 2027 school year. STEM Saturday meets on second Saturdays, 10 am to 12 pm, in the same school year.

cost.text: Families eligible through ELRC or CCIS childcare assistance pay nothing. The programs page does not list any other fee.

first_step.how: Fill in the interest form linked from the programs page for STEM Afterschool or STEM Saturday. The same form is used for all three programs.
first_step.basis: Enrollment for girls in grades 3 to 8 in the service area runs through a public interest form, but the site does not describe a first day or a waitlist.
first_step.what_to_expect: Girls work in teams and on their own on hands-on STEM projects with program staff. STEM Afterschool combines STEM activities, academic support, leadership, and career exploration, and STEM Saturday has a new hands-on theme each month with experiments, engineering or robotics challenges, and coding. Families who qualify for ELRC or CCIS childcare help pay nothing.
first_visit_tips: Check whether your child's school is on the afterschool pickup list, which names William McKinley, Julia de Burgos, Conwell Middle School, Sankofa Freedom Academy, and Mariana Bracetti Academy.
Ask how pickup works, since the programs page does not explain it.
Ask about ELRC or CCIS childcare help when you fill in the interest form, since it can make the program free.

records.notes: The Girls in STEM Summer Institute is described as a 2027 program with details to come, so it is not recorded. The programs page gives no accessibility or language information and no waitlist statement. Pickup procedures are not described. The volunteer page lists four adult roles, recorded only in what_you_do because this record is for the girls' programs. The volunteer page says no minimum age or background check is stated, and it does not say volunteers receive a service-hours letter, so that requirement stays unknown.

records.name: Ethiopian Community Association of Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: Community association for Ethiopians in Greater Philadelphia that shares health and mental health resources, runs a young adults program, and works to keep Ethiopian culture alive for children.
records.what_you_do: Call or email the office to ask how to join, watch for public community celebrations such as the Ethiopian Day festival, or use the contact page to ask how to volunteer.

schedule.text: Office open Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 2 pm. The association's public Ethiopian Day celebration has run for several years, with a September 2025 edition.

cost.text: The site does not state membership dues. Donations are accepted and described as tax deductible.

first_step.how: Call the office Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 2 pm, or email ethcomstaff@gmail.com, and ask how to become a member. Going to a public community celebration is another way to meet members.
first_step.basis: The membership page exists, but it does not say who can join, what the steps are, or what it costs, so the way in is unclear. Public celebrations are announced, and the office has posted hours and a phone line.
first_step.what_to_expect: The office is open Monday to Thursday from 10 am to 2 pm, which is the time to call or visit. Public celebrations have featured music, cultural dance, vendors, and food. The site does not describe membership meetings, dues, or what a new member does, so ask before you join.
first_visit_tips: Call during office hours to confirm how to join, since the membership page does not say.
Ask whether any events are open to people who are not members before you come.

records.notes: The membership page does not say who may join, the steps, or dues. Tier 1 said no membership fee was listed; this record says the site does not state dues instead. The 2026 bylaws PDF in the footer may cover membership, but its URL was not visible, so it was not opened. The May 17, 2026 board election notice, a member-only item, is the last sign of life. Event dates: a festival on September 6, 2025 (12 to 6 pm) and an October 9, 2021 festival at Clark Park. The events page has a second page that was not read. The fetch tool flagged the footer email and phone links as possibly placeholders; the displayed email and phone match tier 1, but verify before the next pass. Two groups named on the health resources page, Ethio Philly Young Adult Association and Ethio Philly Mental Health Council, appear to be the association's own programs and are listed as leads only.

leads_only.name: Ethio Philly Young Adult Association
leads_only.note: Named on the association's health resources page as a young adults resource. It has no separate site that was found, and it was not checked.

leads_only.name: Ethio Philly Mental Health Council
leads_only.note: Named on the association's health resources page as a mental health resource. It has no separate site that was found, and it was not checked.

blocked.note: Redirected to an unrelated domain (pabipemkabngawi.org). The redirect was not followed. This archdiocese ASL schedule page could confirm Epiphany's interpreted Mass times if it can be read another way.
